trust_decision.summary: Ref and symref names advertised by a (possibly hostile) remote are trusted as '/'-separated object-tree paths when getRemoteInfo builds its result; segments like __proto__ or constructor walk out of the result object into Object.prototype.

landing_point.why: Advisory title names getRemoteInfo; the ref-path-to-object-tree loop is the only nested key walk in the function.

fix_sites.entry_point: git.getRemoteInfo (public API) - symrefs loop, fed from symref= capabilities parsed at src/wire/parseRefsAdResponse.js:58-63

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both fixed loops sit in the same function (src/api/getRemoteInfo.js:82-102); the symref loop is a second input source, not an out-of-scope module.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the only adjacent candidate (push result refs map, src/wire/parseReceivePackResponse.js:36), a solver can argue it is a single-level assignment that cannot reach the global Object.prototype and belongs to git.push, not getRemoteInfo.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legal ref names that collide with inherited property names (e.g. a ref segment 'constructor') must still appear in the tree as own properties, and honest refs next to a poisoned one must still be returned; a fix that drops or throws on all such names breaks this (fix test expects info.constructor.prototype.polluted === oid).

O6_input_shapes: __proto__ as intermediate ref path segment (refs loop)
__proto__ inside a symref= capability name (symrefs loop)

O7_producer.where: src/wire/parseRefsAdResponse.js:42-63 builds refs/symrefs Maps from the wire; the fix keeps it unchanged and guards in the consumer

O8_uncovered_routes.route: git.push: server-reported ref name from receive-pack status is used as a key on result.refs, so a '__proto__' ref sets that object's prototype to an object carrying server text (local object poisoning, not global).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Single-level assignment, cannot pollute the global prototype; different command (push) and different sink from the getRemoteInfo ref tree.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other file, src/wire vs src/api; reached via src/commands/push.js:281

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A nested ref-tree view (refs split on '/') in getRemoteInfo2's protocol-v1 branch instead of the flat formatInfoRefs array.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getRemoteInfo2 is the documented successor to getRemoteInfo and a maintainer porting the 'object tree is easier to use' convenience would copy the same loop.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An object-tree output option for listServerRefs built by splitting ref names on '/'.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: listServerRefs already formats the same remote.refs Map; adding a tree mode mirrors getRemoteInfo.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Parsing 'key=a.b' capability values into nested objects.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: v2 capabilities like 'fetch=shallow filter' invite structured parsing into nested objects.

O9_family: prototype pollution (CWE-1321) via server-controlled ref names used as object-tree paths

O10_build.project_tests: __tests__/test-getRemoteInfo.js, __tests__/test-getRemoteInfo2.js; the fix's tests use an in-process mock http client (fix.diff:254-275), so no git-http-mock-server is needed for them.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Skip only parts equal to '__proto__' in the refs loop, missing the symrefs loop and the constructor/prototype inherited-key walk (o[part] || {} returns Object).

out_of_scope_notes: Fix commit f6746a64 is an unrelated feature (AbortSignal for push/http, fix.diff:1-236); only b3db1118 is the security fix.

GitCommit/GitAnnotatedTag parseHeaders assign header keys onto a plain object (src/models/GitCommit.js:80, src/models/GitAnnotatedTag.js:73) but values are strings, so __proto__ assignment is a no-op.
unverified: Latest release is 'none', so present_in_latest is unknown.

single_site flag: the fix touches one function at two loops; the one O8 candidate is a weaker, local-object poisoning on a different sink, so it may not count as a route into the same sink. If it is excluded, O1=1 with no O8 and single_site holds strictly.
Whether the advisory text mentions symrefs was not checked; only the summary was available.
